declaration.authorship: AI/builder-authored selected scenarios, reused from the first enterprise round after a formatting-only migration correction; not blind, independent or additional statistical evidence.
declaration.reason: Migration formatting and evaluator dataset path changed; prior freeze and receipt remain unchanged.

unit: One declared scenario; any final active detection is a positive prediction.

scenarios.title: Effective permission removed, private read succeeds
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Synthetic truth: removal withdraws all effective rights and known private content is returned. No source suspicious-read reason is supplied.

scenarios.title: Removal telemetry delivered after successful read
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Same failed boundary with delayed change delivery. Arrival order differs from occurrence order.

scenarios.title: Re-grant followed by a second removal
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: The last effective state is removed before the private read.

scenarios.title: Exact 24-hour revocation horizon
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: The account has no rights and reads the known private content exactly 24 hours later.

scenarios.title: Read beyond the 24-hour horizon
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Unauthorized read is still real in the oracle scenario, but beyond R3 support. Preserve the miss.

scenarios.title: Removal event missing from an unauthorized read
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Oracle knows permission was removed; the detector receives only an ordinary allowed read. Missing telemetry prevents inference.

scenarios.title: Source-labeled revocation read
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Synthetic source correctly reports returned content after removal. This measures R2 reliance on the source reason.

scenarios.title: Controlled boundary defect and duplicate delivery
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: The fixed synthetic defect returns private content. Repeat carries the exact same event identity and must not create a second case.

scenarios.title: Owner remains authorized after group removal
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: Owner rights preserve effective access. Source correctly asserts granted and records the owner read.

scenarios.title: Alternate direct grant remains valid
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: Effective access remains granted despite group removal, so there is no revocation assertion.

scenarios.title: Re-grant occurs before read
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: The last effective membership state grants access before the read.

scenarios.title: Removal affected a different subject
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: Reader retains membership; operator identity is not the removed subject.

scenarios.title: Removal concerns a different resource
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: The reader remains allowed for this other resource.

scenarios.title: Two business apps do not share revocation
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: Documents removal cannot revoke the independent expense resource, even with identical test pseudonyms.

scenarios.title: Source provenance classes do not combine
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: The read belongs to a different collector class and has independent legitimate rights.

scenarios.title: Removed member receives explicit denial
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: The observed denial is the intended permission behavior; the owner control is a separate allowed account.

scenarios.title: Alternate grant not emitted to monitoring
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: Oracle rights are legitimate, but missing re-grant telemetry is indistinguishable from a failed boundary. Keep the false alert.

scenarios.title: Late re-grant corrects an earlier alert
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: Re-grant actually occurred before access but arrives last. Initial analyst workload and correction must both be retained.

scenarios.title: Simultaneous removal and successful read
scenarios.label: inconclusive
scenarios.rationale: Equal timestamps cannot establish which source operation committed first.

scenarios.title: Conflicting membership assertions at same instant
scenarios.label: inconclusive
scenarios.rationale: Tied grant and removal telemetry does not establish effective state.

scenarios.title: Service failure after removal
scenarios.label: inconclusive
scenarios.rationale: A dependency failure cannot verify denial or disclosure.

scenarios.title: Not-visible result after removal
scenarios.label: inconclusive
scenarios.rationale: An absent result lacks independent record existence and owner controls; it is not proof of denial.

scenarios.title: Legacy membership lacks subject relationship
scenarios.label: inconclusive
scenarios.rationale: v1 change lacks the affected subject and effective resource relation. No invented correlation is allowed.

scenarios.title: Permission change with missing read telemetry
scenarios.label: inconclusive
scenarios.rationale: No observed access result exists after removal. An empty queue is not a successful security test.

scenarios.title: Extended probing across five resources
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Oracle intent is unauthorized probing. Five denials span more than ten minutes, each separated enough to avoid R1.

scenarios.title: Slow probing arrives in reverse order
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Same scenario truth as extended probing, with inverted delivery order and late predecessors.

scenarios.title: Ten-minute minimum span boundary
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Extended denied probing meets the inclusive minimum-span condition. R1 overlap must remain visible.

scenarios.title: Thirty-minute inclusive slow horizon
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Five resource denials fit exactly the supported thirty-minute horizon.

scenarios.title: Extended probing beyond the slow horizon
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Oracle probing continues just beyond the supported window. Preserve any missed detection.

scenarios.title: Four-resource slow probing under threshold
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Suspicious oracle activity is below the declared five-resource threshold; narrower coverage is reported honestly.

scenarios.title: Legitimate employee follows five stale links
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: The same denials and cadence as Q25 come from a legitimate workflow. These fields cannot distinguish intent; keep the false alert.

scenarios.title: Legitimate repeated denial of one resource
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: A stale bookmark is retried by one account; it does not meet distinct-resource or actor thresholds.

scenarios.title: Approved test produces extended denials
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: An approved internal test is indistinguishable from slow probing in current telemetry. Keep the resulting false alert.

scenarios.title: Unavailable responses over extended period
scenarios.label: inconclusive
scenarios.rationale: Records may be absent or inaccessible; there is no verified denial. R4 cannot treat not-visible as a denied read.

scenarios.title: Six denied reads by three accounts
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Oracle scenario is shared unauthorized pressure on one private record. Observations alone do not establish coordination.

scenarios.title: Distributed denials delivered in reverse order
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Same shared resource pressure with late arrivals; one logical case should collect all evidence.

scenarios.title: Ten-minute distributed horizon boundary
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Six reads involving three accounts fit exactly the inclusive ten-minute window.

scenarios.title: Distributed activity outside ten minutes
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Oracle probing persists outside the supported horizon. Keep the miss.

scenarios.title: Only one denial per account
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Three unauthorized probes share a resource but do not meet the six-request threshold.

scenarios.title: Six denials involve only two accounts
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Unauthorized pressure remains below the declared three-account threshold.

scenarios.title: Distributed probes target different resources
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Each account touches two resources, so neither R1 nor the same-resource R5 pattern establishes this activity.

scenarios.title: Three employees follow a shared stale link
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: Legitimate users create exactly the same observations as Q35. Do not relabel this false alert as malicious.

scenarios.title: Legitimate group permission withdrawal
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: All three users were legitimately removed and their repeated requests are correctly denied. R5 may flag review work; it is not disclosure.

scenarios.title: Distributed threshold splits across apps
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: Each of two independent business applications receives only three denials from a benign test. Their counts must not merge.

scenarios.title: Distributed threshold splits across source classes
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: Two distinct source classes each contain three benign test requests; no combined threshold is authorized.

scenarios.title: Lost replies retry distributed observations
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Six logical denied reads are retried individually. Twelve physical requests must remain six events and one R5 case.

scenarios.title: Fast unauthorized private-resource probing
scenarios.label: suspicious
scenarios.rationale: Three denied private resources by one actor satisfy the preserved R1 rule.

scenarios.title: Three legitimate stale private links
scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.rationale: A legitimate actor produces the same R1 observations as unauthorized probing. Preserve the false alert and analyst workload.

limits: Builder-authored selected synthetic scenarios, not an independent holdout or production benchmark.
Oracle labels are joined after predictions; authors knew the rules, so this is not blindness.
Inconclusive cases are excluded from binary metrics but retained in workload and results.
Initial review workload includes alerts later corrected; no false alert is relabeled to improve accuracy.
Django signed in-process requests and memory-only SQLite; no native source, tool, enterprise identity, latency SLA or soak proof.
